bibl.title: Thirst regulates motivated behavior through modulation of brainwide neural population dynamics | Science

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: how a physiological need state is represented across the whole brain and how that representation changes what a sensory cue does
span.quote: However, it is unclear how the activity of these hypothalamic neurons activates and coordinates other brain systems involved in sensation, decision-making, and action in order to produce the appropriate goal-directed behavior. The cellular dynamics of brainwide states underlying basic survival drives have heretofore remained inaccessible.

span.label: how thirst motivation is represented downstream of the dedicated thirst neurons, and how that state regulates sensation and action
span.quote: However, the mechanisms regulating this sensory modulation remain unclear, as does the neural representation of the motivational drive itself.

span.label: a brainwide mode of population activity that encodes motivational state, exists before the cue, and gates whether sensory input propagates into behaviour
span.quote: Water-predicting sensory cues elicited activity that rapidly spread throughout the brain of thirsty animals. These dynamics were gated by a brainwide mode of population activity that encoded motivational state. After satiation, focal optogenetic activation of hypothalamic thirst-sensing neurons returned global activity to the pre-satiation state.

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: Thus, motivational states specify initial conditions that determine how a brainwide dynamical system transforms sensory input into behavioral output.

span.label: thirst motivational state
span.quote: We investigated these questions in the context of thirst, a motivational drive that is essential for survival, is modulated on a rapid time scale, and is implemented by well-characterized neural circuitry.

span.label: electrophysiology
span.quote: While mice performed this task, we used high-density Neuropixels microelectrode arrays ( 24 ) to acutely record single units from many brain regions (listed in table S1 ) distributed across the mouse forebrain and midbrain ( Fig. 1, B and F ).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: The thirst state sets a brainwide landscape of initial conditions, so the same sensory perturbation launches a different activity trajectory depending on the state the brain starts in
span.quote: Our results suggest that the aversive thirst motivational state sets a landscape of “initial conditions,” spread across many brain regions, that determine subsequent sensory stimuli–evoked brainwide neural dynamics.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Thirst imposes persistent pre-cue activity that modulates local circuitry in parallel across the brain, gating whether sensory input is transformed into motor output
span.quote: Through imposing this brain-wide state, thirst establishes persistent activity that exists prior to the animal sensing a water-predicting cue and can then modulate local circuitry in parallel throughout the brain to gate the subsequent transformation of sensory input into motor output in a state-dependent manner.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Hypothalamic thirst-neuron activity is broadcast to downstream circuits through successive fast synaptic transmission and/or neuromodulator release
span.quote: This broadcast may proceed through multiple levels of fast synaptic transmission and/or via neuromodulators, which feature prominently in the regulation of other brainwide arousal states ( 44 ).

span.label: the thirst neuron activity is broadcast to downstream circuits, possibly through multiple levels of fast synaptic transmission or via neuromodulators
span.quote: The brainwide activity mode we identify appears to represent the direct effects of this thirst neuron activity that is broadcast to downstream circuits. This broadcast may proceed through multiple levels of fast synaptic transmission and/or via neuromodulators, which feature prominently in the regulation of other brainwide arousal states

span.label: sensory regions keep responding to the cue whatever the state; what satiety removes is the propagation of that signal past them to motor circuits
span.quote: Although initial sensory regions continue to respond to stimuli with high fidelity regardless of satiety state, the gating conferred by satiety greatly diminishes the propagation of sensory information beyond sensory regions, preventing the activation of motor circuits.

span.label: the state is described as a landscape of initial conditions spread across many regions that determines the trajectory a stimulus sets off
span.quote: Our results suggest that the aversive thirst motivational state sets a landscape of “initial conditions,” spread across many brain regions, that determine subsequent sensory stimuli–evoked brainwide neural dynamics.

span.label: in the sated animal an energetic barrier stops the same stimulus from driving the dynamics down the path to behaviour
span.quote: When the animal is sated, an “energetic barrier” throughout the brain prevents the same stimulus from pushing the dynamics down the same trajectory that leads to behavior.

span.label: satiety does not turn down all cue-responsive neurons together; it acts on particular subclasses of them
span.quote: Satiety state–dependent modulation prior to the onset of behavior is therefore not manifested as a broad change in responsiveness across all cue-responsive neurons, but in fact it specifically modulates the activity of certain subclasses of those neurons

span.label: The functional relevance of the widespread activity patterns is not established
span.note: what this limits: the brainwide activity result: ALTHOUGH THIS ACTIVITY WAS EXTREMELY WIDESPREAD, THE FUNCTIONAL RELEVANCE OF THESE GLOBAL ACTIVITY PATTERNS REMAINS TO BE DETERMINED
span.quote: Although this activity was extremely widespread, the functional relevance of these global activity patterns remains to be determined.

span.label: Probably only a subset of the responsive regions is actually necessary for the task
span.note: what this limits: any necessity claim from the imaging: IT IS LIKELY THAT ONLY A SUBSET OF BRAIN REGIONS ARE NECESSARY FOR TASK PERF[ormance]
span.quote: As was shown in a previous study of large-scale activity during the same task in the mouse neocortex ( 23 ), it is likely that only a subset of brain regions are necessary for task performance, at least in the simplest task conditions.

span.label: Whether the identified mode is thirst-specific or a general arousal signal is unresolved
span.note: what this limits: the thirst-specificity of the mode: IT REMAINS TO BE SEEN WHETHER ... THE THIRST-RELATED MODE WE OBSERVE REPRESENTS A MORE GENERAL FORM [of arousal]
span.quote: It remains to be seen whether other physiological survival-need states modulate different modes of activity, or whether the thirst-related mode we observe represents a more general form of arousal across multiple types of motivation.

span.label: the functional relevance of the brainwide activity is left undetermined even though its existence is the headline
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 0 - the existence is the headline, the relevance is open
span.quote: Although this activity was extremely widespread, the functional relevance of these global activity patterns remains to be determined. As was shown in a previous study of large-scale activity during the same task in the mouse neocortex ( 23 ), it is likely that only a subset of brain regions are necessary for task performance, at least in the simplest task conditions.

span.label: the authors expect only a subset of brain regions to be necessary for the task, so widespread activity is not widespread necessity
span.note: what this limits: which regions are NECESSARY, as against where activity is found - a narrower scope than item 3: the authors expect only a subset of brain regions to be required for the task, so brainwide activity is not brainwide necessity
span.quote: Although this activity was extremely widespread, the functional relevance of these global activity patterns remains to be determined. As was shown in a previous study of large-scale activity during the same task in the mouse neocortex ( 23 ), it is likely that only a subset of brain regions are necessary for task performance, at least in the simplest task conditions.

span.label: the Cue and Behavior modes are named for one thing but may carry reward anticipation, decision-making and motor preparation as well
span.note: what this limits: the names on the two modes, which are hypotheses about what loaded onto them: THE CUE MODE WAS DESIGNED TO CAPTURE ACTIVITY RELATED TO THE SENSORY RESPONSE BUT COULD ALSO INCLUDE SIGNALS RELATED TO REWARD ANTICIPATION, DECISION-MAKING, AND MOTOR PREPARATION
span.quote: The Cue mode was designed to capture activity related to the sensory response but could also include signals related to reward anticipation, decision-making, and motor preparation. The Behavior mode captured activity potentially related to motor output, sensorimotor feedback, and reward anticipation and consumption.

span.label: whether other need states use different modes, or whether this one is general arousal, is left open
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 2 - whether other need states use different modes, or whether this one is general arousal, is left open
span.quote: It remains to be seen whether other physiological survival-need states modulate different modes of activity, or whether the thirst-related mode we observe represents a more general form of arousal across multiple types of motivation.

span.label: stimulation did not restore the thirsty reading everywhere: medial prefrontal and retrosplenial cortex went on decoding sated
span.note: what this limits: the completeness of the state restoration: SEVERAL OF THE HIGHEST-LEVEL CORTICAL REGIONS [medial prefrontal and retrosplenial] CONTINUED TO DECODE THAT THE ANIMAL WAS SATED
span.quote: Several of the highest-level cortical regions [corresponding to medial prefrontal (PL/ ILA) and retrosplenial (RSP) cortex] continued to decode that the animal was sated, consistent with expected access of these regions to contextual or working-memory cues on recent water consumption

span.label: initial conditions, trajectories and an energetic barrier used as the description of a motivational state
span.quote: Our results suggest that the aversive thirst motivational state sets a landscape of “initial conditions,” spread across many brain regions, that determine subsequent sensory stimuli–evoked brainwide neural dynamics.

span.label: the low dimensionality and pervasiveness of brainwide cellular activity during behavior, established in Caenorhabditis elegans and larval zebrafish
span.quote: Our results comport with the low dimensionality and pervasiveness of brainwide cellular activity during behavior in both Caenorhabditis elegans ( 39 ) and larval zebrafish

span.label: spike sorting run through a framework with EXPLICIT DRIFT TRACKING AND CORRECTION
span.quote: To ensure that single units were stably spike-sorted throughout the session, we used a recently developed spike-sorting framework with explicit drift tracking and correction

span.label: the State mode is not a discovered variable but an axis constructed to maximally separate thirsty from sated during the baseline epoch, and the Cue and Behavior modes are defined the same way from their own epochs
span.quote: We defined a “State mode” of activity that maximally separated thirsty and sated states during the baseline epoch, a “Cue mode” that maximally separated activity on Go and No-Go trials during the odor epoch (up to 500 ms after odor onset, before the mouse began licking), and similarly a “Behavior mode” that separated activity on Go and No-Go trials from the response epoch (1 s around time of the reward onset)

span.label: the mode names are declared impure by the authors themselves: the Cue mode may carry decision and motor-preparation signals, so the label names the epoch it was defined in, not the content it holds
span.quote: The Cue mode was designed to capture activity related to the sensory response but could also include signals related to reward anticipation, decision-making, and motor preparation. The Behavior mode captured activity potentially related to motor output, sensorimotor feedback, and reward anticipation and consumption.

span.label: near-orthogonality of the three axes is MEASURED before it is imposed - 82, 84 and 65 degrees prior to orthogonalisation
span.quote: Prior to orthogonalization, the angles between the State axis and the Cue and Behavior axes were 82° and 84°, respectively, and 65° between the Cue and Behavior axes.

span.label: a single unit here is an identity maintained across an hours-long session by drift-tracking software, not by a stable observation
span.quote: To ensure that single units were stably spike-sorted throughout the session, we used a recently developed spike-sorting framework with explicit drift tracking and correction

span.label: the brain-region label on every neuron is derived from the maximal channel on the probe and a registration to a common atlas, so region membership is an inference rather than an observation
span.quote: Neurons were assigned to brain area according to the location of their maximal channel on the electrode array, with location transformed into a common anatomical reference space.

span.label: gating here means diminished propagation beyond sensory regions, not diminished sensory response - the sensory regions themselves keep their fidelity
span.quote: Although initial sensory regions continue to respond to stimuli with high fidelity regardless of satiety state, the gating conferred by satiety greatly diminishes the propagation of sensory information beyond sensory regions, preventing the activation of motor circuits.

span.label: method: high-density extracellular recording across many brain regions during a Go/No-Go task, with population-mode decomposition, linear decoding and optogenetic stimulation
span.note: a second reading DIFFERING from the recorded value. Recorded: electrophysiology — a second reading, verbatim-verified, disagreeing with the value on the record. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: we used high-density Neuropixels microelectrode arrays ( 24 ) to acutely record single units from many brain regions (listed in table S1 ) distributed across the mouse forebrain and midbrain

span.label: phenomenon: state-dependent gating of a water-predicting cue: the same odour produces a brainwide wave when thirsty and only a transient when sated
span.note: a second reading DIFFERING from the recorded value. Recorded: thirst motivational state — a second reading, verbatim-verified, disagreeing with the value on the record. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: When mice were sated, there was still a diminished transient response to the Go and No-Go cues in many regions, but the stimuli failed to produce persistent activity past the sensory cue period

span.label: builds-on → prior brainwide cellular-activity studies in Caenorhabditis elegans (ref 39) and larval zebrafish (ref 40)
span.quote: Our results comport with the low dimensionality and pervasiveness of brainwide cellular activity during behavior in both Caenorhabditis elegans ( 39 ) and larval zebrafish ( 40 ).

span.label: builds-on → a previous large-scale mouse neocortex study using the same task (ref 23)
span.quote: As was shown in a previous study of large-scale activity during the same task in the mouse neocortex ( 23 ), it is likely that only a subset of brain regions are necessary for task performance, at least in the simplest task conditions.

span.label: contradicts → the account in which satiety modulates cue responses as a broad change in responsiveness across all cue-responsive neurons
span.quote: Satiety state–dependent modulation prior to the onset of behavior is therefore not manifested as a broad change in responsiveness across all cue-responsive neurons, but in fact it specifically modulates the activity of certain subclasses of those neurons

span.label: extends → recordings in hungry animals showing gating of responses to food-predicting stimuli in a variety of brain regions
span.quote: A prevalent model is that motivational states regulate behavior by amplifying, in a state-dependent manner, the salience of specific sensory signals that predict reward ( 4 ). Neural recordings in hungry animals found “gating” of responses to food-predicting stimuli, such that responses to these stimuli were greatly diminished when animals were sated versus hungry.

span.label: supports → the classical drive-reduction model of water-seeking behaviour
span.quote: water consumption reduces SFO and MnPO activity ( 19 , 20 ) via activation of local MnPO interneurons ( 21 ), implementing a mechanism akin to the classical “drive reduction” model for regulation of water-seeking behavior

span.label: builds-on → whole-brain cellular recordings in C. elegans and larval zebrafish showing low-dimensional pervasive dynamics
span.quote: Our results comport with the low dimensionality and pervasiveness of brainwide cellular activity during behavior in both Caenorhabditis elegans ( 39 ) and larval zebrafish

span.label: distinguishes-from → the view that a widespread activity pattern is thereby a necessary one
span.note: status: the paper's own words: remains to be determined · differs in: THE AXIS IS WIDESPREAD AGAINST NECESSARY. 'ALTHOUGH THIS ACTIVITY WAS EXTREMELY WIDESPREAD, THE FUNCTIONAL RELEVANCE OF THESE GLOBAL ACTIVITY PATTERNS REMAINS TO BE DETERMINED. As was shown in a previous study ..., IT IS LIKELY THAT ONLY A SUBSET OF BRAIN REGIONS ARE NECESSARY FOR TASK PERFORMANCE.' The paper's own headline observation is separated from the inference a reader would draw from it, BY THE PAPER, before anyone else can draw it. Extent is measured; necessity is not, and the two are different experiments. Q-501.
span.quote: Although this activity was extremely widespread, the functional relevance of these global activity patterns remains to be determined. As was shown in a previous study of large-scale activity during the same task in the mouse neocortex ( 23 ), it is likely that only a subset of brain regions are necessary for task performance, at least in the simplest task conditions.

span.label: satiety state —operationalised-as→ State mode
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — the state is read off one axis of population activity that persists before odour onset
span.quote: Whereas the cue-and behavior-related modes were primarily modulated by the task in a satiety state–dependent manner, activity along the state mode was persistent throughout the trial, including the period before odor onset. Thus, there existed a brainwide representation of satiety state that appeared to gate the flow of activity in response to sensory inputs.

span.label: State mode —contrasted-with→ Cue mode
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — CRITERION: the State mode stays elevated through both trial types while the Cue mode discriminates them and collapses on satiety
span.quote: These three activity modes displayed distinct dynamics and sensitivities to satiety state. The State mode was persistently elevated throughout both Go and No-Go trials when the animal was thirsty and displayed only slight modulation by task engagement ( Fig. 4C , left). By contrast, the Cue mode strongly discriminated between Go and No-Go trials and displayed a large reduction in activity on Go trials upon satiety ( Fig. 4C , center). Finally, the Behavior mode was only substantially activated on thirsty Go trials

span.label: Cue mode —distinct-from→ Behavior mode
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.7 — the authors declare the separation imperfect: both may carry reward anticipation, so the names are epoch labels, not content labels
span.quote: The Cue mode was designed to capture activity related to the sensory response but could also include signals related to reward anticipation, decision-making, and motor preparation. The Behavior mode captured activity potentially related to motor output, sensorimotor feedback, and reward anticipation and consumption.

span.label: odor epoch —operationalised-as→ Cue mode
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — each mode is defined by the epoch it maximally separates in - the definition is temporal, not anatomical
span.quote: We defined a “State mode” of activity that maximally separated thirsty and sated states during the baseline epoch, a “Cue mode” that maximally separated activity on Go and No-Go trials during the odor epoch (up to 500 ms after odor onset, before the mouse began licking), and similarly a “Behavior mode” that separated activity on Go and No-Go trials from the response epoch (1 s around time of the reward onset)

span.label: baseline epoch —operationalised-as→ State mode
span.note: strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: We defined a “State mode” of activity that maximally separated thirsty and sated states during the baseline epoch, a “Cue mode” that maximally separated activity on Go and No-Go trials during the odor epoch (up to 500 ms after odor onset, before the mouse began licking), and similarly a “Behavior mode” that separated activity on Go and No-Go trials from the response epoch (1 s around time of the reward onset)

span.label: gating —causes→ motor circuits
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — SIGN: negative - the gating prevents the activation of motor circuits
span.quote: Although initial sensory regions continue to respond to stimuli with high fidelity regardless of satiety state, the gating conferred by satiety greatly diminishes the propagation of sensory information beyond sensory regions, preventing the activation of motor circuits.

span.label: sensory regions —distinct-from→ gating
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — the sensory regions are the one place the gating does NOT act; their fidelity is preserved across states
span.quote: Although initial sensory regions continue to respond to stimuli with high fidelity regardless of satiety state, the gating conferred by satiety greatly diminishes the propagation of sensory information beyond sensory regions, preventing the activation of motor circuits.

span.label: PIR —part-of→ sensory regions
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — and correspondingly PIR keeps decoding odour identity in all four blocks
span.quote: Olfactory sensory regions (PIR and OLF), while changing in the expected direction in their state decoding, nonetheless continued to decode odor identity with high accuracy across all four trial blocks

span.label: Nos1+ —part-of→ SFO
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — the causal handle is a genetically specified subset, not a region
span.quote: Expression of ChR2-eYFP in Nos1+ SFO neurons.

span.label: drive reduction —operationalised-as→ SFO
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — SIGN: negative - drinking REDUCES activity in this circuit, which is what makes it drive reduction
span.quote: water consumption reduces SFO and MnPO activity ( 19 , 20 ) via activation of local MnPO interneurons ( 21 ), implementing a mechanism akin to the classical “drive reduction” model for regulation of water-seeking behavior

span.label: drive reduction —operationalised-as→ MnPO
span.note: strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: water consumption reduces SFO and MnPO activity ( 19 , 20 ) via activation of local MnPO interneurons ( 21 ), implementing a mechanism akin to the classical “drive reduction” model for regulation of water-seeking behavior

span.label: Neuropixels —operationalised-as→ single units
span.note: strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: we used high-density Neuropixels microelectrode arrays ( 24 ) to acutely record single units from many brain regions (listed in table S1 ) distributed across the mouse forebrain and midbrain

span.label: single units —part-of→ brain region
span.note: strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: we used high-density Neuropixels microelectrode arrays ( 24 ) to acutely record single units from many brain regions (listed in table S1 ) distributed across the mouse forebrain and midbrain

span.label: spike-sorting —operationalised-as→ single units
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — Q-52: the unit's identity over an hours-long session is a guarantee made by drift-tracking software
span.quote: To ensure that single units were stably spike-sorted throughout the session, we used a recently developed spike-sorting framework with explicit drift tracking and correction

span.label: decoders —operationalised-as→ satiety state
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — the per-region decoder is what splits submaximal-everywhere from full-in-a-subset
span.quote: To discriminate these possibilities, we analyzed the predictions of decoders of satiety state and trial type, trained on thirsty and sated data from the activity during the baseline epoch and initial odor response epoch, respectively, of simultaneously recorded neurons in a single region.

span.label: thirst —same-as→ initial conditions
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.8 — a redescription in borrowed vocabulary, not a measurement - the state IS a landscape of initial conditions
span.quote: Our results suggest that the aversive thirst motivational state sets a landscape of “initial conditions,” spread across many brain regions, that determine subsequent sensory stimuli–evoked brainwide neural dynamics.

span.label: thirst —operationalised-as→ Go/No-Go
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — thirst is measured by whether the mouse still works for water in this task
span.quote: We used a head-fixed thirst-motivated olfactory Go/No-Go decision-making task ( 22 , 23 ) to study how thirst motivation regulates sensory processing and behavior in mice

span.label: Wilcoxon signed-rank test
span.quote: * P < 0.05 (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, Bonferroni correction). Data are means ± 95% confidence interval.

span.label: Wilcoxon rank-sum test
span.quote: Task-modulated neurons exhibited substantially better fits to the model than nonmodulated neurons (mean 0.17 ratio of deviance explained for task-modulated versus 0.06 for non–task-modulated, P < 0.001, Wilcoxon rank-sum test; fig. S5D )

span.label: chi-squared test
span.quote: The majority of neurons that decreased their baseline firing rate as the animal transitioned from being thirsty to being sated subsequently increased their firing rate upon stimulation (1195 of 1781,67%), and vice versa for neurons that increased their firing rate upon the transition from thirsty to sated (1003 of 1417, 71%) ( P < 0.05, χ 2 test)

span.label: t-test with false-discovery-rate correction
span.quote: Regions labeled in red have a statistically significant decrease in decoding ( P < 0.05, two-tailed t test, FDR correction across all regions with three or more recordings).

span.label: correlation against shuffled data with Bonferroni correction
span.term: correlation against shuffled data with Bonferroni correction
span.quote: To characterize this modulation, we found neurons throughout the brain with activity during the baseline period that was significantly correlated with the animal’s satiety state over the course of a session ( P < 0.01, absolute R value compared with shuffled data, Bonferroni correction)

span.label: linear decoder (classification analysis)
span.quote: We applied a linear decoding approach to quantify the extent to which activity within each of the three task epochs (baseline, odor, and response) respectively encoded different task elements (satiety state, trial type, and per-trial licking)

span.label: unsupervised clustering
span.quote: Unsupervised clustering of the average activity of task-modulated neurons ( N = 12,986) across the thirsty and sated Go and No-Go trials revealed clusters of neurons with activity that qualitatively appeared to correlate with each of these state, cue, and behavior variables

span.label: held-out test data (out-of-sample validation)
span.quote: Predictions in Thirsty and Sated blocks in (D) and (E) are on held-out test data.

span.label: standard error of the mean
span.quote: Water-restricted mice performed hundreds of trials per session (226 ± 7 trials, mean ± SEM), licking specifically on the Go cue with a near 100% hit rate, until they eventually became sated and stopped responding to the cue

span.label: Wilcoxon signed-rank test
span.quote: The Hit rate was also not significantly different between Thirsty and Stim conditions (97 ± 1% versus 94 ± 2%, P = 0.67, Wilcoxon signed-rank test).

span.label: two-tailed t test
span.quote: In sated mice, the ability to decode odors dropped to near chance levels throughout much of the brain [18/29 regions with >3 recordings per region had significantly changed decoding accuracy; P < 0.05, two-tailed t test, false discovery rate (FDR) correction]

span.label: false discovery rate (FDR) correction
span.quote: In sated mice, the ability to decode odors dropped to near chance levels throughout much of the brain [18/29 regions with >3 recordings per region had significantly changed decoding accuracy; P < 0.05, two-tailed t test, false discovery rate (FDR) correction]

span.label: More than half of the ~24,000 neurons recorded across 34 brain regions changed their firing with the thirst task, responding rapidly to the water-predicting odour cue before sustained water-acquisition activity.
span.quote: We found that more than half of recorded neurons were modulated by this task, with a rapid and widespread response to a water-predicting olfactory cue preceding sustained activity related to water acquisition.

span.label: The rewarded odour cue triggered a wave of activity that started in olfactory regions about 150 ms after odour onset and reached every recorded brain region within about 300 ms.
span.quote: The Go cue produced a wave of activity in thirsty animals that began in olfactory regions within ~150 ms of odor onset and rapidly (within ~300 ms) spread to neurons in every region we recorded from

span.label: Satiety gated the wave: once mice were sated the identical odour cue produced only a brief transient change in firing and no licking.
span.quote: The animal’s satiety state gated this wave of activity: In satiated mice, the same sensory cue produced only a transient change in activity and no behavioral response.

span.label: Spontaneous pre-stimulus baseline firing, not just cue-evoked firing, shifted with satiety state in neurons across many brain regions.
span.quote: Surprisingly, the spontaneous baseline activity of neurons across many brain regions was also modulated by the animal’s satiety state.

span.label: Odour identity could be decoded from populations throughout the brain in thirsty mice, but decoding fell to near chance across much of the brain once the mice were sated.
span.quote: In sated mice, the ability to decode odors dropped to near chance levels throughout much of the brain

span.label: Single neurons were specialised: each mostly encoded one task aspect (state, cue, or behaviour), while every brain region held a mixture of all these neuron types.
span.quote: Each individual neuron primarily encoded one aspect of the task, and every brain region contained a diverse mixture of neurons encoding different aspects of the task.

span.label: Optogenetic stimulation of hypothalamic thirst neurons in sated mice pushed behaviour, within-trial brainwide dynamics, and single-neuron satiety correlates back to their thirsty-state values.
span.quote: We found that this focal stimulation returned the behavior, brainwide single-neuron within-trial dynamics, and brainwide single-neuron correlates of satiety state back to the state corresponding to thirst.

span.label: Re-creating the thirst representation in only a subset of brain regions was enough to restore thirst-motivated sensory processing, behaviour and the associated brainwide dynamics.
span.quote: These results suggest that recapitulation of the thirst state in a subset of regions is sufficient to restore thirst-motivated sensory processing and behavior, along with the associated brainwide activity dynamics.

span.label: the Go cue produced a wave of activity that began in olfactory regions within about 150 ms and reached every recorded region within about 300 ms
span.quote: The Go cue produced a wave of activity in thirsty animals that began in olfactory regions within ~150 ms of odor onset and rapidly (within ~300 ms) spread to neurons in every region we recorded from

span.label: the initial onset and the brainwide propagation of the activity wave both preceded the onset of licking; first licks were measured at 0.86 s after odor onset
span.quote: Both the initial onset and the brainwide propagation of this activity wave substantially preceded the onset of licking (first licks were measured at 0.86 ± 0.04 s after odor onset, mean ± SEM across sessions).

span.label: a large fraction of units in every brain region, 54% of total or 12,986, were modulated by the task
span.quote: A large fraction of these units in every brain region (54% of total; 12,986) were modulated by the task

span.label: in sated mice the cues still produced a diminished transient response but no persistent activity after the cue period
span.quote: When mice were sated, there was still a diminished transient response to the Go and No-Go cues in many regions, but the stimuli failed to produce persistent activity past the sensory cue period

span.label: 35 percent of neurons had spontaneous baseline firing correlated with satiety state, in every brain region
span.quote: we found neurons throughout the brain with activity during the baseline period that was significantly correlated with the animal’s satiety state over the course of a session ( P < 0.01, absolute R value compared with shuffled data, Bonferroni correction) ( Fig. 2E ). These neurons constituted a large fraction of neurons in each brain region ( N = 8395,35% of total

span.label: satiety modulation was not a broad change across all cue-responsive neurons but acted on particular subclasses
span.quote: Satiety state–dependent modulation prior to the onset of behavior is therefore not manifested as a broad change in responsiveness across all cue-responsive neurons, but in fact it specifically modulates the activity of certain subclasses of those neurons

span.label: state-related clusters were barely modulated by the cue and were active throughout the trial on thirsty or on sated trials
span.quote: The state-related clusters ( N = 3484 units, 27% of total) exhibited only slight modulation upon cue presentation but were active throughout the trial selectively on either thirsty or sated trials

span.label: most neurons in most regions were selective for only one of state, cue or behaviour
span.quote: Different brain regions had different fractions of neurons that encoded state-, cue-, or behavior-related features (or combinations thereof) ( fig. S5G ), but the majority of neurons in most regions were selective for only one feature

span.label: the three modes together captured about half the trial-averaged task-related variance across the brain
span.quote: We made use of this temporal separation to define orthogonal modes of population activity that encoded each task element ( Fig. 4A ), which together captured ~50% of the trial-averaged task-related variance throughout the brain.

span.label: ASSUMPTION MEASURED BEFORE IT WAS IMPOSED: the three axes were already near-orthogonal before orthogonalisation, at 82, 84 and 65 degrees
span.quote: Prior to orthogonalization, the angles between the State axis and the Cue and Behavior axes were 82° and 84°, respectively, and 65° between the Cue and Behavior axes.

span.label: the State mode stayed elevated through Go and No-Go trials alike while the animal was thirsty
